# Troubleshooting {#sec-troubleshooting}

A symptom-first index to the rest of the book.

## Login and access

**"Permission denied (publickey)" when I `ssh` — it worked before.**
Your SSH key almost certainly **expired** (they last one year). Regenerate it in the portal's
SSH Key Manager, unzip into `~/.ssh`, `chmod 0600 -R ~/.ssh` (@sec-first-login).

**"Permission denied" on a brand-new setup.**
Check permissions: `chmod 0600 -R ~/.ssh`, and make sure you unzipped the key into `~/.ssh`.
Confirm you're using `medicinebow.arcc.uwyo.edu`, not the dead `southpass` name.

**I can't get an account at all.**
Only a **PI** can request it, in writing, against a project. You cannot self-register
(@sec-account).

**Globus won't let me add the collection.**
If you're an external collaborator on an **ARCC-Only account**, you can't use Globus. You need
a UW-side guest collection (@sec-moving-data).

## Jobs won't submit

**`sbatch: error: ... You have to specify an account.`**
Add `--account=cowy-firesurro` (@sec-anatomy).

**`Job violates accounting/QOS policy (...)` at submit time.**
Your request exceeds a QOS limit (every QOS is `DenyOnLimit`). Usually `--time` exceeds the
QOS ceiling — e.g. 5 days under `normal` (max 3 d). Lower `--time` or switch QOS
(@sec-partitions). Check ceilings with `sqos` and `showuserlimits`.

**`Invalid qos specification`.**
Your account can't use that QOS. Yours are `debug, fast, interactive, long, normal`
(`sacctmgr -n show assoc user=$USER format=qos`).

## Jobs won't start

**Stuck in `PENDING` with reason `Priority`.**
The machine is just busy and you're in line. Either wait, or pick a higher-priority (shorter)
QOS — QOS dominates priority here (@sec-priority). Small/short jobs backfill sooner.

**Stuck with reason `Resources`.**
You asked for a lot (many cores, much memory, a scarce GPU). Right-size (@sec-resources), or
accept the wait. `showjobreasons <id>` explains in plain language.

**GPU job pending for hours.**
H100/L40S are heavily contended (@sec-queue-times). Develop on `mb-a30` instead, and check
`gpuavail`/`showpartitions` for what's actually free before submitting.

**Pending with `QOSMax...` or `AssocGrpCpuLimit`.**
You (or your account) hit a cap — e.g. too many cores in flight at once. Wait for your other
jobs to finish, or throttle an array with `%` (@sec-arrays).

## Jobs fail

**`OUT_OF_MEMORY`.**
Raise `--mem`. Compare `MaxRSS` to `ReqMem` in `sacct` (@sec-fail). Watch the 10 GB/core
default trap (@sec-resources).

**`TIMEOUT`.**
Job outran `--time`. Checkpoint (@sec-checkpointing), raise `--time` within the QOS ceiling,
or split the work into an array.

**`FAILED`, worked interactively but not in batch.**
You loaded modules / activated conda on the login node but not **inside the submit script**.
Put them in the script (@sec-anatomy, @sec-conda).

**Output file references files that "don't exist."**
Relative paths from the wrong directory, or you wrote to `/lscratch` (wiped at job end). Use
absolute paths or `$SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR`; copy `/lscratch` output out before the job ends
(@sec-storage).

**`PREEMPTED` / `REQUEUED` on a long job.**
You were on investor hardware and got reclaimed. Move to `--partition=non-investor` and
checkpoint (@sec-preemption).

## Software

**"That module doesn't exist" but I'm sure it does.**
`module avail` only shows what's reachable now. Use `module spider <name>` — you probably need
to load a compiler first (@sec-modules).

**CUDA won't build / link.**
Load `gcc/13.2.0` (not 14) — `cuda-toolkit` is built against 13.2 despite its deprecation
warning (@sec-modules).

**Home directory full, everything breaking.**
Conda in `/home`. Move envs to `/project/<proj>/software` via `~/.condarc`, and clean up
(@sec-conda). Check with `du -sh ~/* | sort -h`.

**GPU job runs but is slow / `nvidia-smi` shows 0%.**
Your code isn't actually on the GPU. Verify the framework sees CUDA; in a container, you need
`--nv` (@sec-gpu).

## Still stuck?

Email **`arcc-help@uwyo.edu`** with your **job ID**, the submit script, and the error. Or
bring it to **office hours, Tuesdays 11am–1pm** on Zoom. Include what you already tried — it
gets you a faster answer.
